options.why: When the central bank raises rates, borrowing becomes more expensive and may decline. Firms often delay investments.

options.t: Borrowing increases because loans cost less for firms
options.why: Loans cost more, not less, when rates rise. Borrowing tends to fall.

options.t: Borrowing is banned for all businesses by law
options.why: Raising rates does not ban borrowing. It only makes it costlier.

q: Which factor of production includes the tools and machinery used to make goods?

options.t: Land
options.why: Land means natural resources, such as soil and minerals. It is not tools and machinery.

options.t: Capital
options.why: Capital includes tools, machinery and buildings used to make goods. It is a factory's physical equipment.

options.t: Enterprise
options.why: Enterprise is the entrepreneur's initiative and risk taking. It is not the tools themselves.

options.t: Labor
options.why: Labor is human work. Machinery is capital.

q: A tariff is placed on imported steel. What is a likely effect on domestic steel buyers?

options.t: They may pay higher prices for steel
options.why: A tariff raises the price of imported steel. Domestic buyers may pay more for steel, either imported or home-made.

options.t: They will receive steel for free
options.why: Tariffs do not make steel free. They add a tax that raises prices.

options.t: They see imported steel get cheaper
options.why: A tariff makes imports more expensive, not cheaper. Buyers see higher prices.

options.t: They will no longer need any steel
options.why: Steel is still needed. A tariff changes its price, not whether buyers want it.

q: What does a market economy rely on to answer what to produce?

options.t: Traditions passed down for many generations
options.why: Traditions guide a traditional economy. A market economy relies on demand and business choices.

options.t: Random selection of products in the stores
options.why: Random selection is not how markets decide. Demand and profit guide choices.

options.t: Decisions made only by a central planner
options.why: A central planner decides in a command economy. In a market economy, many people decide.

options.t: Consumer demand and the choices of businesses
options.why: A market economy relies on consumer demand and the choices of businesses. Firms produce what customers will pay for.

q: What is globalization?

options.t: A steady decline in international trade between many nations
options.why: Globalization is not a decline in trade. It is a growing connection among nations.

options.t: A tax on all exports sent out of the country by all firms
options.why: A tax on exports is a trade policy. It is not globalization.

options.t: The growing connection of economies through trade and investment
options.why: Globalization is the growing connection of economies through trade and investment. Goods, money and ideas cross borders more freely.

options.t: A rule limiting each country to local goods only, to keep imports out
options.why: A rule limiting countries to local goods is protectionism. It is the opposite of globalization.

q: A bakery doubles its workers in the same small kitchen, but output rises only a little. Which concept applies?

options.t: The law of diminishing returns
options.why: Doubling workers in the same small kitchen raises output only a little. That shows the law of diminishing returns, where each added worker adds less.

options.t: Comparative advantage in trade
options.why: Comparative advantage is about trade between countries. It does not explain a crowded kitchen.

options.t: Economies of scale in a firm
options.why: Economies of scale means costs fall as output grows. Here output barely rises, so it does not apply.

options.t: Price discrimination by firms
options.why: Price discrimination is charging different prices to different buyers. It has nothing to do with workers.

q: What is the role of taxes in the economy?

options.t: They replace the need for money in the whole economy
options.why: Taxes do not replace money. They collect it from people and firms.

options.t: They prevent all business from making a profit in a market
options.why: Taxes do not prevent profit. Businesses still earn profits after taxes.

options.t: They fund government services such as roads and schools
options.why: Taxes fund government services such as roads, schools and safety. They pay for goods the market may not supply well.

options.t: They set the price of every product in the market
options.why: Taxes do not set prices. Markets and firms set most prices.

q: Which statement describes a business cycle?

options.t: A rule about the hours of business for all stores
options.why: A rule about store hours is a regulation. A business cycle is an economic pattern.

options.t: A single period of constant growth with no decline
options.why: Constant growth with no decline is not a cycle. A cycle repeats ups and downs.

options.t: A fixed schedule for opening new stores each year
options.why: A schedule for opening stores is a company plan. It is not an economic cycle.

options.t: Repeating periods of economic expansion and contraction
options.why: A business cycle is repeating periods of economic expansion and contraction. The economy grows, peaks, shrinks and recovers.

q: What is empathy in the workplace?

options.t: Ignoring a coworker's problems to stay on task
options.why: Ignoring coworkers' problems is the opposite of empathy. It shows no care for their feelings.

options.t: Understanding and sharing the feelings of others
options.why: Empathy is understanding and sharing the feelings of others. It improves teamwork and trust.

options.t: Avoiding any emotional conversation with coworkers
options.why: Avoiding emotional conversation is not empathy. Empathy means engaging with feelings.

options.t: Agreeing with everything that others say to you
options.why: Agreeing with everything is not empathy. You can understand without agreeing.

q: A coworker criticizes your idea in a meeting. Which response shows self-control?

options.t: Leave the room and refuse to return
options.why: Leaving the room and refusing to return avoids the issue. It shows poor self-control.

options.t: Say the coworker is not qualified to comment
options.why: Saying the coworker is not qualified attacks the person. It shows poor self-control.

options.t: Stay calm and ask for specific feedback
options.why: Staying calm and asking for specific feedback shows self-control. You manage emotions and learn from the comment.

options.t: Raise your voice and defend yourself
options.why: Raising your voice and defending yourself shows poor control. It escalates the situation.

q: Why is honesty important when you make a mistake at work?

options.t: It builds trust and allows problems to be fixed quickly
options.why: Honesty about a mistake builds trust and lets problems be fixed quickly. Others can help once they know.

options.t: It lets you avoid taking responsibility for the error
options.why: Honesty does not avoid responsibility. It means taking it.

options.t: It makes mistakes unimportant to the rest of the team
options.why: Honesty does not make mistakes unimportant. It helps handle them.

options.t: It guarantees you will never be corrected again by anyone
options.why: Honesty does not guarantee you will never be corrected. Everyone makes mistakes.

options.why: Recognition raises motivation. It does not lower it.

options.why: A schedule for breaks is an HR policy. A code of ethics sets principles.

q: What is a business plan?

q: Why do many new businesses seek a loan or investor?

options.why: A tax-free structure with no owners does not exist. The restaurant has an owner.

options.t: A decline in local jobs as small firms close
options.why: Hiring neighbors adds local jobs. It is not a decline.

q: What is a sole proprietorship?

options.t: A business owned and run by one person

options.t: A business owned by two or more partners
options.why: A business owned by two or more partners is a partnership. A sole proprietorship has one owner.

q: Which is an advantage of owning a franchise?

options.why: Support and a recognized brand from the franchisor are advantages of a franchise. Training and marketing help new owners succeed.

options.t: Guaranteed profit with no risk to the owner at all
options.why: No business is risk free. A franchise does not guarantee profit.

options.t: Freedom to change the products without approval

options.t: No fees ever paid to the franchisor or head office
options.why: Franchisees pay fees and royalties to the franchisor. They are not free.

q: An entrepreneur notices that many customers ask for a service no one nearby provides. What should she do first?

options.t: Open immediately without any research
options.why: Opening immediately without research is risky. It could waste money.

options.why: Ignoring customers' requests wastes an opportunity. They are showing demand.

q: What does innovation mean in business?

options.why: Raising prices without adding value is not innovation. It gives buyers nothing new.

options.t: Copying a competitor exactly with no changes at all
options.why: Copying a competitor exactly is imitation. Innovation adds something new.

options.t: Keeping the same product forever and never changing it

q: Why do entrepreneurs need to understand ethics?

options.why: Honest practices build trust with customers and partners. Trust leads to repeat sales and strong relationships.

q: What is a budget?

options.why: Avoiding records is not the purpose. Information systems keep records.

options.t: To collect, store and provide information for decisions
options.why: An information system collects, stores and provides information for decisions. Managers rely on it to act on facts.

options.t: To replace all employees with machines that run the firm
options.why: An information system does not replace all employees. It supports them.

options.t: To entertain customers while they wait in the store
options.why: Entertaining customers is not its purpose. It manages information.

q: What is data mining?

options.t: Writing code for websites and apps used by a firm
options.why: Writing code is programming. Data mining analyzes data.

options.t: Deleting old files to free up space on the computer
options.why: Deleting old files is housekeeping. Data mining finds patterns.

options.t: Searching large data sets for patterns and insights
options.why: Data mining means searching large data sets for patterns and insights. Businesses use it to spot trends and customer habits.

options.t: Digging for minerals underground with drills and tools
options.why: Digging for minerals is mining in the literal sense. Data mining is digital.

q: A company sells high-end headphones. Which target market is most likely to match the product?

options.t: Businesses that do not use audio in their work
options.why: Businesses that do not use audio will not buy headphones. They are not a match.

options.t: Audio fans who value sound quality and will pay more
options.why: Audio fans who value sound quality and will pay more match high-end headphones. They are the likely target market.

options.t: Shoppers who want only the cheapest option available
options.why: Shoppers who want only the cheapest option will not buy high-end products. They are the wrong target.

options.t: People who never listen to music of any kind at all
options.why: People who never listen to music will not buy headphones. They are not a target.

q: Which factor influences customer buying behavior?

options.t: Needs, income, culture and personal preferences
options.why: Needs, income, culture and personal preferences influence customer buying behavior. They shape what and when people buy.

options.t: Only the weather on the day of the visit to the shop
options.why: Weather can matter, but it is not the only factor. Many influences exist.

options.t: Only the name of the cashier at the front register
options.why: The cashier's name does not drive buying behavior. It is a trivial detail.

options.t: Only the color of the store sign out front
options.why: The sign color is a small factor. Many other things matter more.

q: A company notices younger customers buy mostly through mobile apps. What marketing decision does this support?

options.t: Raising prices for everyone who buys the app
options.why: Raising prices does not respond to the habit. It could push buyers away.

options.t: Stopping all research into what customers want
options.why: Stopping research ignores what customers do. The company should keep learning.

options.t: Removing all digital promotion for newspaper ads
options.why: Removing digital promotion ignores the mobile habit. Young customers are online.

options.t: Improving the mobile app experience and offers
options.why: Improving the mobile app experience and offers fits younger customers who buy through mobile. It meets them where they shop.

q: What is the purpose of market research?

options.t: To avoid learning about customers or about rivals
options.why: Market research is not meant to avoid learning. It aims to learn.

options.t: To set employee schedules for the next work week
options.why: Setting schedules is an HR task. It is not research.

options.t: To gather information about customers and competitors
options.why: Market research gathers information about customers and competitors. It helps a business make informed decisions.

options.t: To pay taxes owed to the state by the firm each year
options.why: Paying taxes is a legal duty. It is not research.

q: A company wants to test a new snack before national launch. What is the best approach?

options.t: Offer samples in a few stores and collect feedback
options.why: Offering samples in a few stores and collecting feedback tests the snack on a small scale. It reveals problems before a national launch.

options.t: Ask only the owner's family and a few friends of theirs
options.why: Asking only family and friends gives biased feedback. They may not be honest.

options.t: Skip testing to save time and launch the snack at once
options.why: Skipping testing risks a costly failure. Testing saves money.

options.t: Launch everywhere without feedback to reach buyers
options.why: Launching everywhere without feedback is risky. Problems would appear everywhere.

q: What does positioning mean in marketing?

options.t: Hiding the brand from the public in order to keep it secret
options.why: Hiding the brand is the opposite of positioning. Positioning builds a brand image.

options.t: Creating a distinct place for a product in customers' minds
options.why: Positioning means creating a distinct place for a product in customers' minds. It sets the product apart from rivals.

options.t: Raising the price of every product that the firm sells
options.why: Raising prices is a pricing decision. It is not positioning.

options.t: Placing a product on the lowest shelf where few customers look
options.why: Placing a product on a low shelf is merchandising. It is not positioning.

q: Why is quality control important in production?

options.t: It eliminates the need for customers
options.why: Quality control does not remove the need for customers. It satisfies them.

options.t: It makes products cost more for no reason
options.why: Quality control does not raise costs for no reason. It prevents bigger losses.

options.t: It slows all delivery down to zero
options.why: It does not slow all delivery to zero. It checks products.

options.t: It helps ensure products meet standards
options.why: Quality control helps ensure products meet standards. It reduces defects and complaints.

q: A factory finds a defect rate increasing each week. What should management do first?

options.t: Stop measuring defects in the factory
options.why: Stopping measurement hides the problem. It makes things worse.

options.t: Ignore the defects until customers complain
options.why: Ignoring defects until customers complain damages reputation. Act early.

options.t: Blame the workers without checking first
options.why: Blaming workers without checking is unfair. The cause may be in the process.

options.t: Investigate the cause and fix the process
options.why: Investigating the cause and fixing the process addresses the root problem. It stops defects from rising.

q: What is the purpose of a safety training program?

options.t: To increase sales and the firm's profits
options.why: Safety training is not meant to raise sales. Its goal is protection.

options.t: To prevent accidents and injuries at work
options.why: A safety training program prevents accidents and injuries at work. It teaches safe methods and awareness.

options.t: To avoid keeping records of any accidents
options.why: Avoiding records of accidents is wrong. Records help improve safety.

options.t: To reduce the number of employees paid
options.why: It does not cut employees. It protects them.

q: What is the supply chain?

options.t: A list of company policies for the staff to read and follow
options.why: A list of company policies is a handbook. The supply chain moves products.

options.t: A chain of stores with the same name in many cities
options.why: A chain of stores is a retail group. The supply chain is a network.

options.t: The network that moves a product from supplier to customer
options.why: The supply chain is the network that moves a product from supplier to customer. It includes sourcing, making, storing and delivering.

options.t: The company's bank accounts and the cash held in them
options.why: Bank accounts are finances. The supply chain is not about cash.

q: A supplier's delivery is delayed, and the factory will run out of parts. Which action best reduces this risk in the future?

options.t: Use more than one reliable supplier
options.why: Using more than one reliable supplier spreads risk. If one is delayed, another can deliver.

options.t: Rely on one supplier with no backup
options.why: Relying on one supplier with no backup leaves the factory exposed. It repeats the risk.

options.t: Buy parts only on the last day needed
options.why: Buying parts on the last day needed leaves no buffer. A delay would stop production.

options.t: Stop tracking all inventory levels
options.why: Stopping tracking of inventory removes visibility. It makes shortages likelier.

q: What is project management?

options.t: Planning and controlling work to meet goals on time and in budget
options.why: Project management is planning and controlling work to meet goals on time and in budget. It uses schedules, resources and monitoring.

options.t: Setting prices for products sold by a firm to its customers
options.why: Setting prices is pricing. Project management organizes work.

options.t: Selling products to customers in a store and recording the sales
options.why: Selling products is sales. It is not managing projects.

options.t: Writing a company's mission statement for its own website
options.why: Writing a mission statement is a single task. It is not project management.

q: What does it mean to follow security procedures at work?

options.t: Ignore visitors' badges when they come into the building
options.why: Ignoring visitor badges weakens security. Procedures require checking them.

options.t: Leave doors unlocked to save time, so staff can move freely
options.why: Leaving doors unlocked puts property at risk. Procedures require locking.

options.t: Share passwords with coworkers to be helpful to them
options.why: Sharing passwords breaks security rules. It risks company data.

options.t: Protect company information and property by following rules
options.why: Following security procedures protects company information and property. Everyone must follow the rules.

q: A manager asks employees to organize tasks by urgency and importance. What skill is this practicing?

options.t: Product pricing
options.why: Product pricing is setting prices. Ordering tasks is prioritizing.

options.t: Customer segmentation
options.why: Customer segmentation groups customers. It does not order tasks.

options.t: Prioritizing work
options.why: Organizing tasks by urgency and importance is prioritizing work. It ensures the most critical tasks come first.

options.t: Ad design work
options.why: Ad design is creative work. It is not task ordering.

q: What is overhead in a business?

options.t: The profit left after taxes are paid by the firm
options.why: Profit after taxes is net income. Overhead is an ongoing cost.

options.t: Ongoing costs not tied to one product, such as rent
options.why: Overhead is ongoing costs not tied to one product, such as rent and utilities. It must be paid however much is made.

options.t: The price customers pay for goods in a store or shop
options.why: The price customers pay is revenue. Overhead is a cost.

options.t: The cost of materials for one item, which rises per unit
options.why: The cost of materials for one item is a direct or variable cost. Overhead is not tied to one product.

q: Which action shows good time management?

options.t: Planning tasks by priority and deadlines
options.why: Planning tasks by priority and deadlines is good time management. It makes sure the most important and urgent work gets done first and on time.

options.t: Starting many tasks without finishing them
options.why: Starting many tasks without finishing them spreads effort thin and leaves nothing completed. Good time management means finishing work, not just beginning it.

options.t: Ignoring deadlines set by the manager
options.why: Ignoring deadlines set by the manager causes late work and lost trust. Time management means respecting deadlines and planning backward from them.

options.t: Doing every task at the last minute
options.why: Doing every task at the last minute leaves no time for checking or for surprises. It is procrastination, the opposite of managing time well.

q: What belongs on a résumé?

options.t: Your bank balance and the amount of money you have saved
options.why: A bank balance and savings are private financial details. Employers do not need them, and they have no place on a résumé.

options.t: Contact details, education, work experience and skills
options.why: A résumé should list contact details, education, work experience and skills. Together they show an employer who you are and what you can do.

options.t: A list of everything you dislike about past jobs
options.why: Listing what you dislike about past jobs is negative and unprofessional. A résumé should highlight strengths and achievements instead.

options.t: Your passwords for all of your online accounts and apps
options.why: Passwords are private and must never be shared. Putting them on a résumé would create a serious security risk and does not help your application.

q: After a job interview, what is a good next step?

options.t: Post complaints about the company online
options.why: Posting complaints about the company online looks unprofessional and could end your chance at the job. Employers often search social media.

options.t: Call repeatedly each hour until they answer
options.why: Calling every hour is pushy and annoying. It suggests poor judgment and will probably hurt rather than help your chances.

options.t: Ignore the opportunity and never follow up
options.why: Ignoring the opportunity and never following up wastes a chance to show interest. A short follow-up keeps you on the employer's mind.

options.t: Send a thank-you message to the interviewer
options.why: A thank-you message shows appreciation, restates your interest and leaves a good final impression. It is a standard professional courtesy after an interview.

q: Why is networking useful for a career?

options.t: It replaces the need for skills on the job entirely
options.why: Networking cannot replace job skills. Contacts may open doors, but you still need the ability to do the work once you are hired.

options.t: It guarantees a promotion within a year of joining
options.why: No amount of networking guarantees a promotion in a year. It creates chances and advice, but results depend on performance.

options.t: It helps you learn about opportunities and get advice
options.why: Networking helps you learn about opportunities and get advice. Contacts can share job leads, mentor you and introduce you to useful people.

options.t: It prevents you from changing jobs at all once you start
options.why: Networking does not stop you changing jobs. If anything, it makes moving to a better job easier because more people know you.

q: What does professionalism include?

options.t: Arriving late without notice and leaving early
options.why: Arriving late without notice and leaving early shows a lack of reliability. Professionalism means being punctual and communicating about absences.

options.t: Gossiping about coworkers behind their backs
options.why: Gossiping behind coworkers' backs damages trust and teamwork. Professional people keep conversations respectful and avoid spreading rumors.

options.t: Reliability, respect and appropriate appearance
options.why: Professionalism includes reliability, respect and appropriate appearance. Together they build trust with coworkers, managers and customers.

options.t: Ignoring workplace rules and company policies
options.why: Ignoring workplace rules and policies is unprofessional. Following them shows responsibility and keeps the workplace fair and safe.

q: An employee wants to advance to a manager role. Which step would best support this goal?

options.t: Build leadership skills through training and experience
options.why: Building leadership skills through training and experience prepares someone for a manager role. It shows readiness and gives the employee the abilities managers need.

options.t: Hide accomplishments from supervisors and other staff
options.why: Hiding accomplishments keeps supervisors from seeing your value. Promotion usually depends on visible results, so sharing success is important.

options.t: Stop learning new skills and stay in the same role
options.why: Staying in one role and not learning new skills limits growth. Managers need broader knowledge, so continuing to learn matters.

options.t: Avoid taking on any new responsibilities at work
options.why: Avoiding new responsibilities leaves you with no chance to show leadership. Taking on more is how people prove they are ready to advance.

q: Why should workers continue learning throughout their careers?

options.t: Change never affects any business at all
options.why: Change does affect nearly every business, whether through technology, markets or rules. That is why workers need to keep learning.

options.t: Industries and technology change over time
options.why: Industries and technology change over time, so skills can become outdated. Continuing to learn keeps workers useful and employable throughout a career.

options.t: Training prevents all mistakes at the firm
options.why: Training does not prevent all mistakes. It reduces them, but no amount of learning removes every error.

options.t: Learning ends once a person has a job
options.why: Learning does not end once a person has a job. Workplaces keep changing, so successful people keep building skills for many years.

q: A small bakery learns a large supermarket is adding an in-store bakery. In a SWOT analysis, this is a:

options.t: Chance
options.why: A chance is an opportunity, a favorable outside factor. A new competitor entering your market is an unfavorable outside factor, so it is not a chance.

options.t: Strength
options.why: A strength is an internal advantage of the business. The supermarket is an outside force, so it cannot be one of the bakery's strengths.

options.t: Weakness
options.why: A weakness is an internal problem, such as poor equipment. The supermarket's plan comes from outside the bakery, so it is not a weakness.

options.t: Threat
options.why: A threat is an outside factor that could harm the business. A big supermarket adding an in-store bakery may take customers from the small bakery.

q: What is the manager's role in controlling?

options.t: Compare results with goals and take corrective action
options.why: In controlling, managers compare results with goals and take corrective action when there is a gap. This keeps the organization on track toward its objectives.

options.t: Choose employees' lunch times and assign parking spaces
options.why: Choosing lunch times and parking spaces are minor administrative tasks. They are not the core controlling function of comparing results with goals.

options.t: Print company brochures for the sales team to hand out
options.why: Printing brochures is a routine marketing task. It does not involve measuring results against goals.

options.t: Set the company's logo and the colors used in its ads
options.why: Setting a logo and ad colors is a branding decision. Controlling is about monitoring performance and correcting problems.

q: What is risk management?

options.t: Taking every risk without thought, hoping some pay off
options.why: Taking every risk without thought is reckless. Risk management means weighing risks carefully rather than gambling on luck.

options.t: Hiding risks from owners and all of the other managers
options.why: Hiding risks from owners and managers prevents anyone from preparing. Risk management depends on open sharing of information.

options.t: Identifying and reducing possible threats to a business
options.why: Risk management is identifying and reducing possible threats to a business. It protects assets, people and profits from avoidable harm.

options.t: Ignoring risks to save time and money for the firm
options.why: Ignoring risks leaves the business exposed. A problem that could have been prevented may become expensive later.

q: A company buys insurance to cover possible fire damage. Which risk management strategy is this?

options.t: Accepting the risk
options.why: Accepting a risk means choosing to bear the loss yourself. Buying insurance does not do that; it hands the cost to an insurer.

options.t: Avoiding all risk
options.why: Avoiding risk means not doing the risky activity at all. The company still operates, so it is not avoiding the fire risk.

options.t: Ignoring risk
options.why: Ignoring risk is doing nothing about it. Buying insurance is a deliberate action to deal with the danger.

options.t: Transferring risk
options.why: Buying insurance transfers the financial risk of fire damage to the insurer. The company pays a premium and the insurer covers the loss.

q: Which is a goal that follows the SMART guideline?

options.t: Make more money someday in the near future
options.why: Making more money someday is vague, with no number or date. A SMART goal must be specific and measurable.

options.t: Increase online sales by 10% within six months
options.why: Increasing online sales by 10 percent within six months is specific, measurable and time-bound. It fits the SMART guideline.

options.t: Improve a little bit over the coming months
options.why: Improving a little bit over the coming months has no measure or deadline. It cannot be checked, so it is not SMART.

options.t: Be the best at everything in the whole industry
options.why: Being the best at everything in the industry is not realistic or measurable. SMART goals are achievable and specific.

q: What are the four functions of management?

options.t: Saving, spending, lending and then borrowing
options.why: Saving, spending, lending and borrowing are money actions. They are not the functions of management.

options.t: Buying, selling, hiring and firing workers
options.why: Buying, selling, hiring and firing are business tasks. They are not the four standard functions of management.

options.t: Planning, organizing, leading and controlling
options.why: The four functions of management are planning, organizing, leading and controlling. Together they describe how managers set direction and get results.

options.t: Writing, reading, speaking and listening each week
options.why: Writing, reading, speaking and listening are communication skills. They are not the management functions.

q: A software firm hires a freelancer to design its app, but the written contract never mentions who owns the finished design. What is the safest way to avoid a later ownership dispute?

options.t: State in the contract who owns the intellectual property
options.why: Stating in the contract who owns the intellectual property settles the question clearly in writing. It prevents a later dispute over the finished design.

options.t: Rely on a verbal comment made at the first meeting
options.why: A verbal comment at a meeting is hard to prove later. Ownership should be written in the contract.

options.t: Assume the freelancer keeps all ownership by default
options.why: Assuming the freelancer keeps ownership by default is risky. Rules vary, so the parties should state the agreement in writing.

options.t: Wait until the app is finished and then decide who owns it
options.why: Waiting until the app is finished to decide ownership invites conflict. Both sides will have a stake in the result, so decide beforehand.

q: What does an NDA (non-disclosure agreement) protect?

options.t: An employee's right to a raise in pay each year
options.why: A raise in pay is a compensation matter. An NDA concerns keeping information private, not an employee's earnings.

options.t: A building from fire damage and other harm to it
options.why: Protection from fire damage comes from insurance. An NDA is a legal agreement about secrecy.

options.t: A product from being sold overseas, as export control
options.why: Controls on selling products overseas are export rules. An NDA does not deal with exports.

options.t: Confidential business information from being shared
options.why: An NDA protects confidential business information from being shared. The people who sign agree not to reveal secrets such as plans or customer lists.

q: A customer signs up for a free trial that turns into a paid subscription without a clear warning. Which concern does this raise?

options.t: Import licensing rules for foreign goods
options.why: Import licensing concerns bringing foreign goods into a country. A hidden paid subscription is a consumer protection matter.

options.t: Deceptive or unfair business practices
options.why: Turning a free trial into a paid subscription without a clear warning is a deceptive or unfair practice. Consumer protection law requires clear disclosure.

options.t: Zoning restrictions on where a shop may be
options.why: Zoning rules control where a shop may be located. They have nothing to do with hidden subscription charges.

options.t: Overtime violations, such as unpaid hours
options.why: Overtime violations involve unpaid extra hours for employees. The scenario concerns customers, not workers.

q: Why must a business collect and pay sales tax correctly?

options.t: It is optional for small shops with very low sales
options.why: Sales tax is not optional for small shops. Businesses must collect and send it whatever their size, depending on local rules.

options.t: It is required by law and noncompliance brings penalties
options.why: Collecting and paying sales tax is required by law, and not doing so brings penalties. Fines or legal action can follow errors.

options.t: It increases the store's profit margin as it is added
options.why: Sales tax is collected from customers and passed on, so it does not add to profit. Keeping it would be illegal.

options.t: It replaces income tax entirely for the whole business
options.why: Sales tax does not replace income tax. A business may owe both, since they are separate taxes.

q: An employee posts false claims on social media that damage a competitor's reputation. Which legal issue could result?

options.t: Defamation
options.why: Defamation is making false statements that damage someone's reputation. Posting false claims about a competitor can lead to a lawsuit.

options.t: Trademark
options.why: A trademark protects a brand name or logo. It does not cover false statements about a rival.

options.t: Zoning
options.why: Zoning concerns where and how land can be used. It is unrelated to damaging a competitor's reputation.

options.t: Bankruptcy
options.why: Bankruptcy is a legal process for debts. It is not the issue when someone posts false claims.

q: What is the main purpose of workplace safety regulations?

options.t: To control product prices in all of the shops
options.why: Controlling product prices is not the purpose of safety rules. Safety regulations focus on protecting workers.

options.t: To restrict which customers may shop there
options.why: Safety rules do not decide which customers may shop. They deal with conditions for employees.

options.t: To limit how much employees may earn a year
options.why: Limiting what employees earn is a wage matter. Safety regulations are about preventing harm.

options.t: To protect employees from hazards and injury
options.why: Workplace safety regulations protect employees from hazards and injury. They set standards for equipment, training and conditions.

q: What does 'bankruptcy' allow a person or business to do?

options.t: Avoid all future taxes, so none are paid
options.why: Bankruptcy does not erase future taxes. It deals with existing debts, and taxes still apply afterwards.

options.t: Ignore all contracts that the person has signed
options.why: Bankruptcy does not let someone ignore contracts. It is a legal process, with rules for how debts are handled.

options.t: Seek legal relief from debts they cannot pay
options.why: Bankruptcy lets a person or business seek legal relief from debts they cannot pay. A court oversees the process, which can cancel or reorganize some debts.

options.t: Borrow without limits from any lender at all
options.why: Bankruptcy does not give unlimited borrowing. A bankruptcy record usually makes borrowing harder.

q: A landlord refuses to rent to a business owner because of the owner's religion. What is this?

options.t: Unlawful discrimination
options.why: Refusing to rent because of religion is unlawful discrimination. Anti-discrimination laws protect people from unfair treatment based on religion.

options.t: A lawful marketing move
options.why: Turning someone away for religion is not marketing. It is unequal treatment that the law forbids.

options.t: A normal pricing decision
options.why: A pricing decision is about charging a fee. Refusing service for religion is discrimination, not pricing.

options.t: A required zoning rule
options.why: A zoning rule controls land use. It does not allow a landlord to refuse a tenant for religion.

q: What is a contract's consideration?

options.t: A polite thank-you note after signing
options.why: A thank-you note is a courtesy. Consideration is value exchanged in a contract.

options.t: A discount offered after a complaint is filed
options.why: A discount after a complaint is a customer service gesture. It is not consideration in the contract sense.

options.t: A background check on all of the signers
options.why: A background check is a screening step. It is not consideration.

options.t: Something of value exchanged by each party
options.why: Consideration is something of value exchanged by each party. It can be money, goods, services or a promise, and it makes a contract binding.

q: A manager must tell employees that bonuses will be smaller this year. Which approach is best?

options.t: Hide the reason and say nothing to the staff about it at all
options.why: Hiding the reason and saying nothing breeds rumors and distrust. Employees should hear the news from the manager directly.

options.t: Blame another department in public for all the lost bonuses
options.why: Blaming another department in public is unfair and divisive. It harms morale and avoids responsibility.

options.t: Explain the reasons honestly and respectfully, and allow questions
options.why: Explaining the reasons honestly and respectfully, and allowing questions, treats employees as adults. It keeps trust even when the news is bad.

options.t: Announce it by anonymous note and leave before any questions
options.why: An anonymous note and leaving before questions is cowardly and disrespectful. Employees deserve a chance to ask.

q: What is the purpose of an agenda for a meeting?

options.t: To prove the meeting was held on the right date
options.why: An agenda does not prove a meeting date. Its job is to plan the topics and keep discussion focused.

options.t: To list topics and keep the discussion on track
options.why: An agenda lists topics and keeps the discussion on track. Everyone knows what will be covered and can prepare in advance.

options.t: To record each person's salary and job title
options.why: Salaries and job titles are HR records. They do not belong on a meeting agenda.

options.t: To list items to buy for the office this month
options.why: A shopping list for the office is not an agenda. Agendas list meeting topics.

q: A customer service rep must explain a complicated policy to a confused customer. What is the best technique?

options.t: Read the policy aloud with no examples given
options.why: Reading the policy aloud with no examples does not help a confused customer. The policy is hard to follow, so it needs explaining.

options.t: Speak much faster so the call ends sooner
options.why: Speaking faster makes confusion worse. A confused customer needs a slower, clearer explanation.

options.t: Use plain language and check for understanding
options.why: Plain language and checking for understanding help the customer follow the policy. The rep can ask questions to confirm they understood.

options.t: Use technical terms to show your expertise
options.why: Technical terms to show expertise add to confusion. The goal is to be understood, not to impress.

q: Which format is most appropriate for a formal job application?

options.t: A voicemail with no job details
options.why: A voicemail with no job details gives the employer nothing to consider. A formal application should be written and clear.

options.t: A business letter with a résumé
options.why: A business letter with a résumé is the standard format for a formal application. It is professional and gives the employer what they need.

options.t: A text message full of emojis
options.why: A text full of emojis is too casual for a formal application. It would look unprofessional.

options.t: A short social media post online
options.why: A short social media post is not a formal application. Employers expect a proper document.

q: Two team members misunderstand each other because one used slang the other did not know. What barrier does this show?

options.t: A language barrier
options.why: A language barrier occurs when words or slang are not understood by the listener. Unfamiliar slang is a common example.

options.t: A distance barrier
options.why: A distance barrier involves physical space between people. The problem here was the words used.

options.t: A time-zone barrier
options.why: A time-zone barrier arises when people work in different time zones. It does not describe confusion over slang.

options.t: A hardware barrier
options.why: A hardware barrier concerns equipment failure. The misunderstanding came from language, not machines.

q: Why is proofreading important before sending a business message?

options.t: It makes a message longer than it needs to be
options.why: Proofreading does not aim to make a message longer. It checks for mistakes.

options.t: It guarantees a reply from the reader right away
options.why: Proofreading cannot guarantee a reply. Replies depend on the reader.

options.t: It removes the need for a clear purpose or aim
options.why: Proofreading does not remove the need for a purpose. A message still needs a clear aim.

options.t: It catches errors that could hurt credibility
options.why: Proofreading catches errors that could hurt credibility. A clean message shows care and professionalism.

q: What is the best way to give constructive criticism?

options.t: Speak in vague general terms about the work done
options.why: Vague, general comments do not help someone improve. People need to know what to change.

options.t: Be specific, respectful and focus on improvement
options.why: Constructive criticism is specific, respectful and focused on improvement. It tells the person what to do better and treats them with respect.

options.t: Focus only on personal traits rather than the work
options.why: Focusing on personal traits is unfair and hurtful. Criticism should address the work, not the person.

options.t: Criticize in front of the team so all learn from it
options.why: Criticizing in front of the team humiliates the person. Constructive feedback is usually given in private.

q: A customer says an item arrived broken and wants a refund. The store policy allows exchanges only. What is the best action?

options.t: Offer the exchange, explain the policy and escalate for a possible exception
options.why: Offering the exchange, explaining the policy and escalating for a possible exception respects the rules and tries to help the customer. It may win a refund with approval.

options.t: Give a refund without checking policy, since the customer is always right
options.why: Giving a refund without checking policy ignores company rules. The customer is important, but staff should follow procedures.

options.t: Refuse and end the conversation right away and say nothing more about the problem
options.why: Refusing and ending the conversation leaves a customer with a broken item and no help. It damages the relationship.

options.t: Say the customer surely must have broken it on the way home from our store
options.why: Accusing the customer of breaking it is rude and unfair. It assumes the worst without evidence.

q: How can a business show it values customers' time?

options.t: Add more steps to every purchase
options.why: Adding steps to every purchase wastes customers' time. It shows the business does not value it.

options.t: Delay replies to emails from customers
options.why: Delaying replies to emails frustrates customers. Prompt replies show respect for their time.

options.t: Reduce waiting and respond promptly
options.why: Reducing waiting and responding promptly shows respect for customers' time. It makes service quicker and more pleasant.

options.t: Close the checkout lanes at busy times
options.why: Closing checkout lanes at busy times creates long lines. That wastes customers' time.

q: A call center agent receives a hostile caller. Which response best keeps the call professional?

options.t: Match the caller's anger and raise your own voice right back
options.why: Matching the caller's anger and raising your voice escalates the conflict. It makes a professional resolution much harder.

options.t: Argue about who is correct so the caller learns respect
options.why: Arguing about who is correct wastes time and increases tension. The goal is to solve the problem.

options.t: Hang up immediately without helping the caller in any way
options.why: Hanging up without helping abandons the customer. It would anger them further and harm the company.

options.t: Stay calm, acknowledge the frustration and focus on a solution
options.why: Staying calm, acknowledging the frustration and focusing on a solution keeps the call professional. The caller feels heard and the problem can move forward.

q: What does it mean to 'go the extra mile' for a customer?

options.t: Promise things you cannot deliver
options.why: Promising things you cannot deliver sets up disappointment. Going the extra mile means delivering real value.

options.t: Avoid helping customers in the store
options.why: Avoiding helping customers is the opposite of going the extra mile. It shows no effort.

options.t: Do more than the customer expects
options.why: Going the extra mile means doing more than the customer expects. It builds loyalty and delight.

options.t: Do only what the policy requires
options.why: Doing only what policy requires is the minimum. The extra mile means going beyond it.

q: Why should employees know company policies?

options.t: So they can change them freely at any time
options.why: Employees cannot change policies freely. Policies are set by management.

options.t: So they can explain them accurately to customers
options.why: Employees need to know company policies so they can explain them accurately to customers. This avoids confusion and mistakes.

options.t: So they can hide them from customers who ask
options.why: Hiding policies from customers is dishonest. Customers should be told the rules.

options.t: So they can ignore them when they are busy
options.why: Ignoring policies when busy leads to inconsistent service and errors. Staff should follow policy at all times.

q: A company surveys customers and learns that many dislike the long checkout process. What should it do?

options.t: Blame the customers for being so impatient
options.why: Blaming customers for impatience does not solve the problem. It makes the business look defensive.

options.t: Ignore the survey results and change nothing
options.why: Ignoring survey results wastes useful feedback. The business asked, so it should act on the answers.

options.t: Make the checkout longer so it looks careful
options.why: Making checkout longer makes the complaint worse. Customers already dislike the delay.

options.t: Study the process and find ways to speed it up
options.why: Studying the checkout process and finding ways to speed it up responds directly to the feedback. It improves the customer experience.

q: Which action builds trust with customers?

options.t: Keeping promises about price, quality and delivery
options.why: Keeping promises about price, quality and delivery builds trust. Customers learn they can rely on the business.

options.t: Hiding fees from customers until the time of payment
options.why: Hiding fees until payment is deceptive. It destroys trust.

options.t: Changing prices without notice on each visit
options.why: Changing prices without notice makes customers feel cheated. It erodes trust.

options.t: Ignoring customer questions about the product
options.why: Ignoring questions about the product leaves customers unsure. It shows poor service.

q: What is a customer complaint a chance to do?

options.t: Prove the customer wrong in front of others
options.why: Proving the customer wrong in front of others shames them. A complaint is not a contest.

options.t: Avoid the customer so they stop complaining
options.why: Avoiding the customer leaves the problem unsolved. It does not make the complaint go away.

options.t: Learn and improve the product or service
options.why: A complaint is a chance to learn and improve the product or service. It shows what customers care about and what to fix.

options.t: Lower the quality of service to save money
options.why: Lowering service quality to save money makes problems worse. Complaints should lead to improvement.

q: A drought reduces the supply of wheat. What is the most likely effect on the price of bread?

options.t: It will not change
options.why: A drought reduces wheat supply, so costs rise. Bread prices would not stay unchanged.

options.t: It will tend to rise
options.why: When wheat supply falls, wheat becomes scarcer and costlier. Bread prices tend to rise because bakers pay more.

options.t: It will tend to fall
options.why: Prices tend to fall when supply rises. A drought reduces supply, so the effect is the opposite.

options.t: It will become zero
options.why: Bread would not become free. Scarcer wheat raises costs, so prices go up.

q: What does a trade deficit mean?

options.t: Imports exceed exports
options.why: A trade deficit means imports exceed exports. The country buys more from abroad than it sells.

options.t: Exports exceed imports
options.why: When exports exceed imports, a country has a trade surplus. That is the opposite of a deficit.

options.t: Taxes exceed spending
options.why: Taxes exceeding spending is a budget surplus. It is not about trade.

options.t: Prices fall in the economy
options.why: Falling prices describe deflation. A trade deficit is about imports and exports.

q: Which situation best shows a negative externality?

options.t: A shop sells goods at a profit to local people
options.why: A shop selling goods at a profit to local people is an ordinary transaction. No outside party bears a cost.

options.t: A bakery's smell attracts customers who buy bread
options.why: A bakery's smell attracting customers is a positive externality for neighbors. It benefits others without payment.

options.t: A school raises its tuition fees every year
options.why: A school raising tuition affects the people who pay it. It is not a cost imposed on outsiders.

options.t: A factory pollutes a river used by nearby towns
options.why: A factory polluting a river harms nearby towns who did not choose it. That is a negative externality, a cost imposed on others.

q: What does the unemployment rate measure?

options.t: The share of older people who retire from work in a given year
options.why: The share of older people who retire is a retirement rate. The unemployment rate counts jobless people who want work.

options.t: The share of the labor force that is jobless and looking for work
options.why: The unemployment rate measures the share of the labor force that is jobless and looking for work. It shows how many people cannot find jobs.

options.t: The share of firms that fail each year in a given country
options.why: Firms failing each year is a business failure rate. It is not the unemployment rate.

options.t: The share of workers who earn the minimum wage in a country
options.why: Workers earning the minimum wage is a wage statistic. It does not measure unemployment.

q: Why might a government use subsidies?

options.t: To collect more taxes from firms and from all the families
options.why: Subsidies give money to producers. They do not collect more taxes from firms.

options.t: To prohibit business activity in sectors that the state dislikes
options.why: Subsidies do not prohibit business activity. They support it.

options.t: To encourage certain activities by lowering costs for producers
options.why: Subsidies encourage certain activities by lowering costs for producers. Governments use them to support industries such as farming and clean energy.

options.t: To raise prices on all goods sold in the whole economy today
options.why: Subsidies lower costs and prices. They do not raise prices on all goods.

q: What is a free enterprise system?

options.t: An economy where private owners run businesses for profit
options.why: A free enterprise system is an economy where private owners run businesses for profit. Competition and consumer choice guide what is produced.

options.t: An economy with no money used for any kind of trade at all
options.why: Money is used in free enterprise. An economy with no money would rely on barter.

options.t: An economy where the government owns all and sets prices
options.why: Government ownership of everything is a command economy. Free enterprise relies on private owners.

options.t: An economy without any competition between private firms
options.why: Free enterprise has competition between private firms. It does not remove competition.

q: A teammate takes credit for your idea in front of the manager. What is the most mature first response?

options.t: Embarrass the teammate in a meeting so all see
options.why: Embarrassing the teammate in a meeting is immature and escalates conflict. It does not address the problem constructively.

options.t: Spread rumors about the teammate to the whole team
options.why: Spreading rumors is unprofessional and damages relationships. It harms your reputation as well.

options.t: Refuse to work with anyone on the team again
options.why: Refusing to work with anyone ever again overreacts. It harms the team and your own career.

options.t: Calmly speak with the teammate privately about it
options.why: Calmly speaking with the teammate privately is mature. It lets you clear up the issue without public conflict.

q: What does being adaptable at work mean?

options.t: Adjusting to new situations and changes
options.why: Being adaptable means adjusting to new situations and changes. Adaptable people stay flexible when plans shift.

options.t: Refusing to try any new methods at work
options.why: Refusing new methods is the opposite of adaptable. It shows inflexibility.

options.t: Complaining whenever the plans change
options.why: Complaining whenever plans change shows resistance. Adaptable people cope with change.

options.t: Avoiding all change at the workplace
options.why: Avoiding all change is not adaptable. Adaptable employees embrace it.

q: How does teamwork benefit a business?

options.t: It removes the need for leaders in the whole firm
options.why: Teamwork does not remove the need for leaders. Teams still need direction.

options.t: Combining skills helps solve problems and reach goals
options.why: Teamwork combines skills, which helps solve problems and reach goals. People with different strengths cover for each other.

options.t: It makes work slower in every case, as people talk too much
options.why: Teamwork does not slow work in every case. Good teams often finish faster.

options.t: It ensures nobody ever makes any mistakes at the firm
options.why: Teamwork cannot ensure nobody makes mistakes. It helps catch them.

q: A manager is stressed and snaps at an employee. Later, the manager apologizes. What does this show?

options.t: Weak leadership that should be hidden
options.why: Weak leadership is not what an apology shows. Apologizing is a sign of strength.

options.t: A way to avoid all feedback at work
options.why: An apology does not avoid feedback. It accepts responsibility.

options.t: Accountability and respect for others
options.why: Apologizing after snapping shows accountability and respect for others. It repairs trust and sets a good example.

options.t: A need to avoid the employee for a while
options.why: Avoiding the employee does not fix the harm. An apology does.

q: What does integrity mean?

options.t: Hiding mistakes from the boss and from the whole team
options.why: Hiding mistakes is the opposite of integrity. Integrity means honesty.

options.t: Doing whatever is easiest for you at the time
options.why: Doing whatever is easiest is convenience. Integrity means choosing what is right.

options.t: Following rules only when observed by a manager
options.why: Following rules only when observed is not integrity. It depends on being watched.

options.t: Doing the right thing even when no one is watching
options.why: Integrity means doing the right thing even when no one is watching. It shows honest, consistent character.

q: Which behavior shows respect for coworkers' ideas?

options.t: Interrupting to share an idea
options.why: Interrupting to share your idea cuts others off. It shows poor respect for their ideas.

options.t: Dismissing ideas without thought
options.why: Dismissing ideas without thought shows disrespect. Everyone's ideas deserve a fair hearing.

options.t: Laughing at unusual suggestions
options.why: Laughing at unusual suggestions mocks the person. It discourages sharing.

options.t: Listening without interrupting
options.why: Listening without interrupting respects coworkers' ideas. It tells them you value what they say.

q: A coworker is struggling with a heavy workload. Which response shows empathy and teamwork?

options.t: Take credit for their work and say nothing to them
options.why: Taking credit for their work is dishonest and harms them. It shows no empathy.

options.t: Ask what help they need and offer support when possible
options.why: Asking what help they need and offering support shows empathy and teamwork. It lightens the load and builds trust.

options.t: Tell them to work harder and stop complaining to you
options.why: Telling them to work harder dismisses their struggle. It shows no care.

options.t: Report them to the manager without speaking to them first
options.why: Reporting them without speaking to them first is unfair. A kind talk should come first.

q: What is conflict resolution?

options.t: Finding a fair solution to a disagreement
options.why: Conflict resolution means finding a fair solution to a disagreement. It lets people move forward and keeps relationships healthy.

options.t: Avoiding all discussion of the problem
options.why: Avoiding all discussion leaves the problem unresolved. It tends to grow.

options.t: Winning an argument at any cost to be right
options.why: Winning an argument at any cost is not resolution. It leaves the other side resentful.

options.t: Punishing everyone involved in the dispute
options.why: Punishing everyone does not solve the dispute. It creates more conflict.

q: A founder cannot afford to hire a full-time employee. Which choice would best control costs while still getting help?

options.t: Close the whole business for good now
options.why: Closing the business is an extreme response to a hiring problem. It does not control costs while getting help.

options.t: Hire five full-time workers right away
options.why: Hiring five full-time workers adds big costs the founder cannot afford. It does not match the budget.

options.t: Hire a part-time worker or freelancer
options.why: A part-time worker or freelancer gives help at lower cost. The founder pays only for the work needed.

options.t: Do nothing and let the work pile up
options.why: Doing nothing lets work pile up and hurts the business. It does not solve the problem.

q: What is a start-up cost?

options.t: A tax refund from the state for the firm
options.why: A tax refund is money returned to a taxpayer. A start-up cost is an expense to launch.

options.t: A profit from the first sale of goods
options.why: A profit from the first sale comes after launch. Start-up costs come before.

options.t: A discount for loyal customers each month
options.why: A loyalty discount is a marketing reward. It is not a start-up cost.

options.t: An expense needed to launch a business
options.why: A start-up cost is an expense needed to launch a business. Examples are equipment, licenses, deposits and initial stock.

q: What does a unique selling proposition (USP) describe?

options.t: What makes a product different from competitors
options.why: A USP describes what makes a product different from competitors. It gives customers a reason to choose it.

options.t: The location of the store and its opening hours
options.why: Store location and hours are practical details. They are not a USP.

options.t: A discount on all items sold at the store today
options.why: A discount is a short-term promotion. It does not describe what makes a product unique.

options.t: The cost to produce a product, including materials
options.why: The cost to produce is a financial figure. It is not a USP.

q: A new café owner has few savings and wants to test demand before opening a full shop. What is a smart first step?

options.t: Buy new equipment for ten locations
options.why: Buying equipment for ten locations spends large sums before demand is known. It is risky for someone with few savings.

options.t: Run a small pop-up stand or market booth
options.why: A small pop-up stand or market booth tests demand at low cost. It lets the owner learn what customers want before investing more.

options.t: Hire a large staff before selling anything
options.why: Hiring a large staff before selling anything adds costs without proof. It is risky.

options.t: Sign a long expensive lease immediately
options.why: Signing a long expensive lease commits money before demand is known. It is risky.

q: What is a limited liability company (LLC)?

options.t: A business that cannot ever earn any profit at all
options.why: An LLC is able to earn profit. It is a legal form for a business.

options.t: A business owned by the government, run for the public
options.why: A business owned by the government is a public enterprise. An LLC is private.

options.t: A business form that protects owners' personal assets
options.why: An LLC is a business form that protects owners' personal assets. Owners are usually not personally liable for business debts.

options.t: A business with no owners and no legal form at all
options.why: An LLC is a legal form with owners called members. It does have owners.

q: Why is record keeping important for a small business?

options.t: It tracks income and expenses and supports tax filing
options.why: Record keeping tracks income and expenses and supports tax filing. It shows how the business is doing and helps with decisions.

options.t: It hides money from lenders to qualify for bigger loans
options.why: Hiding money from lenders is dishonest. Good records should be accurate.

options.t: It prevents all competition from other small firms
options.why: Records cannot prevent competition. They help manage the business.

options.t: It makes customers buy more from the whole business
options.why: Record keeping does not make customers buy more. It supports management.

q: An entrepreneur wins a contract that doubles her workload. Which action best manages growth?

options.t: Promise quick delivery with no plan to win more cash now
options.why: Promising quick delivery with no plan risks failing the customer. Growth needs planning.

options.t: Ignore deadlines and hope that things all work out fine
options.why: Ignoring deadlines and hoping risks missing them. The contract may be lost.

options.t: Plan resources, staffing and cash flow before accepting more
options.why: Planning resources, staffing and cash flow before accepting more prevents overload. It lets the business grow without failing.

options.t: Cancel all other customers to focus on the new contract
options.why: Cancelling other customers loses stable business. It puts all her income in one contract.

q: A store's net income is $12,000 on sales of $120,000. What is its profit margin?

options.why: 1% would need net income of $1,200 on $120,000 of sales. The actual figure is higher.
Profit margin is net income divided by sales. $12,000 divided by $120,000 is 0.10, or 10%.
100% would mean all sales were profit. Net income is only part of sales.
12% takes the 12,000 as a percentage. The margin is $12,000 divided by $120,000, which is 10%.

q: What is a liability?

options.t: Money received from customers for sales
options.why: Money received from customers for sales is revenue. A liability is something owed.

options.t: Something a business owns and can use
options.why: Something a business owns and can use is an asset. A liability is the opposite.

options.t: Profit left over after all taxes
options.why: Profit left over after taxes is net income. A liability is a debt.

options.t: An amount a business owes to others
options.why: A liability is an amount a business owes to others. Examples are loans and accounts payable.

q: What is the purpose of savings?

options.t: To avoid earning interest, as cash is safer
options.why: Savings do earn interest, usually. Avoiding interest is not the purpose.

options.t: To raise debt so the person owes more later
options.why: Raising debt is borrowing. Savings are set aside, not borrowed.

options.t: To spend more today than the person earns
options.why: Spending more than you earn leads to debt. Savings help avoid it.

options.t: To set money aside for future needs or goals
options.why: The purpose of savings is to set money aside for future needs or goals. It prepares for emergencies and planned purchases.

q: A person earns $3,000 per month and spends $3,300. What is the likely result?

options.t: Debt or reduced savings
options.why: Spending $3,300 on $3,000 of income leaves a gap of $300 a month. The person must borrow or use savings.

options.t: A guaranteed pay raise
options.why: A pay raise is decided by the employer. Spending more does not earn one.

options.t: A growing savings balance
options.why: Savings grow when income exceeds spending. Here spending exceeds income.

options.t: No effect on finances
options.why: Spending more than income affects finances. It leads to debt or lower savings.

q: What does APR stand for?

options.t: Average payment record
options.why: Average payment record is not what APR stands for. APR is a standard lending term.

options.t: Annual profit ratio
options.why: Annual profit ratio is not the meaning. APR relates to loans, not profit.

options.t: Annual percentage rate
options.why: APR stands for annual percentage rate. It shows the yearly cost of borrowing, including interest and some fees.

options.t: Account payment reserve
options.why: Account payment reserve is not the meaning. APR is annual percentage rate.

q: Why compare interest rates before choosing a loan?

options.t: Loans have no costs at all for the borrower
options.why: Loans do have costs, mostly interest and fees. Comparing rates shows which loan costs less.

options.t: A lower rate reduces the total cost of borrowing
options.why: A lower rate reduces the total cost of borrowing. Comparing rates helps you choose the cheaper loan.

options.t: Rates have no effect on the cost of a loan
options.why: Rates directly affect the cost of a loan. A higher rate means paying more.

options.t: A higher rate always means better service for you
options.why: A higher rate does not mean better service. It means higher cost.

q: An investor puts all her savings into one company's stock. Which risk is she most exposed to?

options.t: Too many different assets
options.why: Having too many different assets is diversification, which reduces risk. She has the opposite situation.

options.t: Interest-free borrowing
options.why: Interest-free borrowing is not a risk of her situation. She is investing, not borrowing.

options.t: A lack of diversification
options.why: Putting all savings into one stock exposes her to a lack of diversification. If that company fails, she could lose everything.

options.t: Excess cash on hand at home
options.why: Excess cash at home is not her problem. She put money into one stock.

q: What is gross pay?

options.t: Total earnings before deductions
options.why: Gross pay is total earnings before deductions. Taxes and other deductions are taken out afterward.

options.t: Pay left over after all taxes
options.why: Pay left after taxes is net pay. Gross pay is before deductions.

options.t: Benefits paid by the employer
options.why: Employer benefits are separate from pay. Gross pay is the paycheck total before deductions.

options.t: A bonus paid only once a year
options.why: A bonus paid once a year is only part of earnings. Gross pay includes all earnings.

q: A business has high sales but is always short of cash. Which is a likely cause?

options.t: Sales are too high to record in the books
options.why: High sales are not too high to record. Cash problems arise from timing.

options.t: Expenses are never paid by the firm at all
options.why: Expenses are paid by firms. Not paying them is not the cause here.

options.t: Profit always equals the cash on hand
options.why: Profit does not always equal cash on hand. Cash timing can differ from profit.

options.t: Customers pay slowly while bills are due
options.why: When customers pay slowly while bills are due, cash runs short even with high sales. Sales on credit are not cash yet.

q: A company wants applicants of many backgrounds. Which recruiting practice would help most?

options.t: Skip job descriptions and hire the first person who applies
options.why: Skipping job descriptions and hiring the first applicant limits diversity and fairness. It is not an effective practice.

options.t: Advertise openings through many channels and communities
options.why: Advertising openings through many channels and communities reaches a wide pool of applicants. It helps attract people from many backgrounds.

options.t: Hire only through personal referrals from current staff
options.why: Hiring only through referrals from current staff tends to repeat the same backgrounds. It limits variety.

options.t: Post openings in one small place that few people see
options.why: Posting in one small place few people see limits the applicant pool. It would not attract many backgrounds.

q: Why do employers conduct background checks?

options.t: To avoid interviews and hire people at random
options.why: Background checks do not replace interviews. They verify information.

options.t: To verify information and reduce hiring risks
options.why: Background checks verify information and reduce hiring risks. They confirm details such as work history or criminal records.

options.t: To lower employee pay and cut the wage bill
options.why: Background checks do not cut wages. They check candidates.

options.t: To advertise jobs on the radio and in the news
options.why: Advertising jobs is recruitment. Background checks verify candidates.

q: An employee repeatedly arrives late. What is the best first step for a supervisor?

options.t: Fire the employee without any discussion at all
options.why: Firing without discussion is harsh for a first step. A conversation should come first.

options.t: Ignore the behavior and hope that it stops soon
options.why: Ignoring lateness lets it continue. A supervisor should address it.

options.t: Embarrass the employee in front of the team
options.why: Embarrassing the employee in front of the team is unprofessional. Handle it privately.

options.t: Discuss the problem and set clear expectations
options.why: Discussing the problem and setting clear expectations is the fair first step. It gives the employee a chance to improve.

q: What does the term 'benefits' mean in compensation?

options.t: Non-wage rewards such as insurance or paid leave
options.why: Benefits are non-wage rewards such as insurance or paid leave. They add to total compensation beyond pay.

options.t: A customer discount given at the cash register
options.why: A customer discount is a sales offer. It is not an employee benefit.

options.t: The company's profits at the end of each year
options.why: Company profits are results. Benefits are rewards to employees.

options.t: The employee's job title, listed on the contract
options.why: A job title is a position name. It is not a benefit.

q: A hacker sends an email pretending to be a bank and asks employees to enter passwords. What is this attack called?

options.t: Encryption
options.why: Encryption protects data by scrambling it. It is not an attack.

options.t: Compression
options.why: Compression shrinks files. It is not a scam.

options.t: Phishing
options.why: Phishing is an attack where someone pretends to be a trusted source to steal information such as passwords. The fake bank email is a classic example.

options.t: Backing up
options.why: Backing up is copying data for safety. It is not an attack.

q: A manager receives sales data in a long table and wants to spot trends quickly. What should she create?

options.t: A memo, no numbers
options.why: A memo with no numbers will not show trends. She needs the data in visual form.

options.t: A staff name list
options.why: A staff list would not show sales trends. It lists names.

options.t: A chart or graph
options.why: A chart or graph shows trends at a glance. It turns a long table into a picture that is easy to read.

options.t: A bigger table
options.why: A bigger table adds more numbers. It does not make trends easier to see.

q: What is the purpose of a firewall?

options.t: To design websites for the firm's brand
options.why: Designing websites is a creative and technical task. A firewall is a security tool.

options.t: To block unauthorized access to a network
options.why: A firewall blocks unauthorized access to a network. It filters traffic to keep out attackers.

options.t: To speed up a printer so pages come out
options.why: Speeding up a printer is a hardware matter. A firewall does not do that.

options.t: To delete old emails from the mail system
options.why: Deleting old emails is mailbox cleanup. A firewall protects the network.

q: A grocery store notices shoppers buy more when products are displayed at eye level. This is an example of:

options.t: Using product placement to influence buying
options.why: Displaying products at eye level uses product placement to influence buying. Items that are easy to see are more likely to be picked.

options.t: Setting a price ceiling to keep food costs low
options.why: A price ceiling is a legal limit on prices. It does not describe shelf placement.

options.t: Hiring more cashiers to work the registers
options.why: Hiring cashiers is a staffing decision. It is unrelated to shelf height.

options.t: Reducing store hours on weekdays and weekends
options.why: Reducing store hours is a scheduling choice. It does not explain the display effect.

q: What is word-of-mouth marketing?

options.t: Paid TV commercials bought each evening
options.why: TV commercials are paid advertising. Word of mouth is free and personal.

options.t: A paid billboard on a busy highway nearby
options.why: A billboard is paid advertising. Word of mouth comes from customers.

options.t: A coupon sent in the mail to your home
options.why: A coupon in the mail is direct marketing. It is not word of mouth.

options.t: Customers telling others about a business
options.why: Word-of-mouth marketing is customers telling others about a business. Personal recommendations are trusted and cost little.

q: What is a loss leader?

options.t: A product sold only to employees at a deep discount
options.why: A product sold only to employees is an employee perk. A loss leader aims at customers.

options.t: A product that cannot be sold in any store or shop
options.why: A product that cannot be sold anywhere is not a loss leader. Loss leaders are sold.

options.t: A product sold at a low price to attract customers
options.why: A loss leader is a product sold at a low price to attract customers. The store hopes they buy other items too.

options.t: A product that is always given away for free
options.why: A product always given away is a freebie. A loss leader is sold, usually at a loss.

q: A company runs the same ad on TV, social media and in stores with the same message and look. What is this practice called?

options.t: Integrated marketing communications
options.why: Using the same message and look across TV, social media and stores is integrated marketing communications. It makes the brand consistent.

options.t: Backward integration of supplies
options.why: Backward integration is owning suppliers. It is not about advertising.

options.t: Market segmentation for the firm
options.why: Market segmentation is dividing customers into groups. The company uses one message everywhere.

options.t: Price skimming strategy for a launch
options.why: Price skimming is a pricing tactic. It does not describe consistent advertising.

q: What does a product's life cycle describe?

options.t: The time it takes to make an item in the factory from start to end
options.why: The time to make an item is production time. A life cycle covers a product's time on the market.

options.t: The stages a product goes through from introduction to decline
options.why: A product's life cycle describes the stages from introduction to decline. The stages are introduction, growth, maturity and decline.

options.t: The length of a product warranty period in months or years
options.why: A warranty period is a length of coverage. It is not a life cycle.
